newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia airport to issue 2.2 bln rgt Islamic bonds.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia airport to issue 2.2 bln rgt Islamic bonds.

text.p: Malaysia's new Kuala Lumpur International Airport Bhd (KLIA) is planning to raise 2.2 billion ringgit ($887 million) from two Islamic bond issues, bank treasury dealers said on Thursday.

They said the first tranche of five-year bonds to raise 1.1 billion ringgit would be issued this month. The second tranche would be issued in April and would have a seven-year tenure, the dealers said.
This will be KLIA's second Islamic bond issue to fund the nine billion ringgit airport, being built 70 km (44 miles) southwest of the capital, Kuala Lumpur.

In January last year, KLIA issued 20-year bonds to raise 2.2 billion ringgit in the biggest single Islamic issue in the country so far. It was also the first Islamic paper to be traded in the local secondary market.
Dealers said the government-backed KLIA was issuing Islamic instruments as part of the Moslem country's efforts to promote Kuala Lumpur as an Islamic financial centre.
Unlike conventional bonds, Islamic debt instruments do not pay a coupon.
Under Islam's Shariah principles, business should be done on the basis of the sale and purchase of assets. Giving loans by charging interest is considered usury.
The religion forbids investing in traditional banks, gaming and liquor companies.

However, Islamic issues, for calculation purposes, carry an internal rate of return (IRR). The first tranche of five-year KLIA bonds is expected to be issued with an IRR of 7.6 percent, the dealers said.
"The IRR and price in the market will depend on what the bond's features are," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
While the bond may not qualify for liquid asset status under local banking regulations, the two bond issues are guaranteed by the government, the dealers said.

Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd has been appointed the facilitating agent for the issue. It is also the joint arranger along with DCB-Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd, KAF Discounts Bhd and PhileoAllied Capital Bhd, the bank dealers said.
Bank Islam and KLIA officials declined comment saying no agreement for the issues had been signed yet.
The sources said an agreement between the arrangers and KLIA would be signed on January 25 at the Ministry of Finance before the Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
KLIA has also sought withholding tax exemption for foreign investors in the bonds. The instruments are expected to be exempted from banks' eligible liabilities criteria, the dealers said.
Malaysia requires its financial institutions to maintain a certain percentage of their deposits and other liabilities in liquid, or easily tradeable, assets, usually government paper.
Eligible liabilities are deposits, investments and other outstandings of an institution. Institutions must maintain a certain percentage of their eligible liabilities as reserves.
The dealers said the government had cleared the first KLIA bond issue as a 16-year facility.
"This would allow KLIA, depending on its need, to reissue the bond at the end of the five-year period," one dealer said.
In January last year, KLIA had said it had already raised 3.3 billion ringgit and needed to raise four billion more to fund the airport project.
($1=2.48 ringgit)
